sourcedFrom: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b (2022)
cleanIntro: The PDP F-Series is its own book, not a footnote in the PDP manual, and the differences matter at the bench. It is a 15-round 9mm in 3.5" and 4" barrels with a glass-fibre reinforced frame, Small and Medium backstraps and a 65 mm trigger reach. Its slide comes apart as one section, its extractor pin turns 90 degrees with a screwdriver instead of drifting straight through, and the recoil spring assembly goes back in opposite ways depending on which barrel length you own.

steps.title: Read the barrel length — it changes the reassembly
steps.action: Establish which F-Series you have from the specification table: 3.5" (89 mm barrel, 172 mm overall, 660 g) or 4" (102 mm barrel, 184 mm overall, 680 g). Both are 9mm x 19, both hold 15 rounds. Note it now.
steps.prose: The two lengths field strip identically but do not reassemble identically, and that is the single fact this pistol punishes you for not knowing. Everything else on the two guns is shared — the same polygonal 250 mm right-hand twist, the same 3.7 mm sight widths, the same reversible magazine release, the same Small or Medium backstrap options. A threaded-barrel F-Series is 15 mm longer than the table figure in both barrel and overall length, with a half-inch by 28 UNEF thread. Write the length on the range bag if you own both.
steps.aside: The F-Series frame is glass fibre reinforced high-strength polymer, unlike the standard PDP's plain high-strength polymer. Solvent discipline matters more, not less.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 6 Technical Specifications, printed p.26 (PDF p.26)

steps.title: Magazine out, then rack and lock open
steps.action: Finger off the trigger and outside the guard, muzzle safe, press the magazine release and remove the magazine. Then grip the rear slide serrations, draw the slide fully rearward in one brisk stroke, and let it ease forward slightly while pressing up on the slide stop so it locks open.
steps.prose: The F-Series magazine release is reversible and sits on the side of the grip, so it drops the magazine cleanly — put the magazine well out of reach of the bench, because the strip ends in a trigger press. The rack must be brisk and complete; a tentative stroke lets the extractor drag the case back rather than throwing it. Do not cover the ejection port with the supporting hand while you do it. The slide stop is easier to engage if you let the slide creep forward a few millimetres from its rearmost point first.
steps.quote: Lock the slide in the open position by allowing the slide to move slightly forward from the rearmost position while pressing upward on the slide stop (3.1 Figure 3).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 3.1 Inspecting the Pistol, printed p.10 (PDF p.10)

steps.title: Chamber, magazine well and bore — all three
steps.action: With the slide locked open, verify the chamber is unloaded, look down through the empty magazine well, and check the bore visually that it is clean, dry and free of any obstruction.
steps.prose: The F-Series shares the PDP's extractor-as-indicator, and it is no more trustworthy here than there — solvent and residue hide the colour, so read the chamber rather than the paint. The bore check earns its place on a pistol that may have been stored oiled: oil standing in a polygonal bore raises pressure the next time it is fired. Run a finger into the chamber if the light is bad. Walther requires this whole sequence every time the pistol changes hands, is transported, is stored or is cleaned.
steps.quote: Check the chamber to verify that it is unloaded and check the bore visually that it is clean, dry, and free from any obstructions (3.1 Figure 4).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 3.1 Inspecting the Pistol, printed p.10 (PDF p.10)
steps.warn: Never rely on mechanical features alone. Walther's line is that the safety of the firearm rests on your handling of it.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, trigger fully to the rear
steps.action: Close the slide by pulling it slightly rearward and releasing it slowly. Point the pistol in a safe direction and squeeze the trigger fully to the rear.
steps.prose: The take-down catch on an F-Series will not depress with the striker cocked, so this press is a mechanical requirement, not a convention. It is also the moment the manual reserves its strongest warning for: a live round left in the chamber discharges here. Walther asks for a visual inspection of both the chamber and the magazine well immediately beforehand — do both, in that order, with the muzzle still pointed somewhere safe. The trigger breaks at about 25 N with a 6 mm travel, shorter than the standard PDP's 9 mm.
steps.quote: Point the pistol in a safe direction. Squeeze the trigger fully to the rear.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)
steps.warn: To complete disassembly you will be required to pull the trigger. Inspect the chamber and the magazine well to be sure they are empty before your finger moves.

steps.title: Take-down catch down, slide off the front
steps.action: Grip the take-down catch from above, one finger each side, press it straight down, and hold it there while you run the slide forward off the frame.
steps.prose: Both sides must be loaded together or the catch cants in its slot and refuses to move — pressing harder on one side achieves nothing but sore fingers. Approaching from above keeps your hand behind the muzzle line while the slide travels forward. Once the catch drops, the slide leaves the rails with no resistance at all and there is nothing to arrest it, so keep hold of it. The F-Series is a small pistol and its slide is correspondingly light and easy to drop.
steps.quote: Move the slide forward, and remove it from the frame.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Recoil assembly out, barrel out — and remember which way round it sat
steps.action: Turn the slide over, lift the recoil guide rod assembly out from under the barrel while taking up the spring pressure, then lift the barrel from the slide. Note which end of the recoil assembly sat at the muzzle.
steps.prose: The assembly is captive but loaded, so ease the rear end out of the barrel recess rather than pulling it — pull and the spring flicks it out of your hand. Noting the orientation now saves the single most common F-Series reassembly error, because the correct orientation is not the same on the two barrel lengths. The barrel then lifts straight out with nothing retaining it. You should have four parts: frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil guide rod assembly from below the barrel while taking up the spring pressure (4.1.1 Figure 2).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: 3.5" and 4" F-Series take the recoil spring in OPPOSITE ways
steps.action: Before you put anything back: on a 3.5" pistol the LARGER end of the recoil spring assembly goes into the spring mounting at the front of the slide. On a 4" pistol the SMALLER end of the recoil rod goes into that same mounting. Then in both cases the rear end goes into the lower barrel recess while you compress the spring.
steps.prose: This is the F-Series' own trap and it is printed nowhere else — the standard PDP book gives one orientation for every gun it covers, the F-Series book gives two. Fitting it the wrong way round on a 3.5" will feel almost right and will bind the slide, which reads as a gritty rail or a short-stroking gun rather than as an assembly error. Check the barrel stamp before you decide which way it goes. Flex in the assembly as it seats is normal, so do not take flex as evidence you have it right.
steps.quote: Insert the recoil spring assembly: 3.5” pistol models: Insert the larger end of the recoil spring assembly into the spring mounting at the front of the slide. 4” pistol models: Place the smaller end of the recoil rod into the spring mounting at the front of the slide.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.1.2 Field-Stripping Reassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)
steps.warn: The 3.5" F-Series and the 4" F-Series are not interchangeable here. Read the barrel length off your own pistol.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring assembly. That is the published F-Series field strip; the slide assembly, the magazine and the preventive spring replacement are the deeper procedures.
steps.prose: Check the set against the main-components figure before any solvent is opened. From here the routine clean covers the bore from the chamber end, the breech face, the chamber end of the barrel, the extractor and adjacent surfaces, and the frame — the parts a range session actually fouls. The striker channel stays out of it because it takes no lubricant. If you need to get into the slide, the F-Series route is section 4.2 and it needs 1 mm and 2 mm drift punches plus a screwdriver.
steps.quote: The main components of the pistol are shown in 4.1.1 Figure 3.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)

deepSteps.title: End cap: punch, 1.5 mm of travel, then pull it down
deepSteps.action: Stand the slide on its muzzle on a smooth flat surface and grip it at the rear serrations. Push a 2 mm drift punch in against the spring pressure through the ROUND opening of the slide end cap, and while keeping downward pressure, slide the end cap down about 1.5 mm. Put the punch down and pull the end cap the rest of the way out.
deepSteps.prose: The F-Series end cap has a round opening, not the square one on the standard PDP, and it comes off in two movements rather than one — a short shift while the punch holds the spring, then a straight pull once the punch is out. Trying to do it in a single stroke is what makes people think it is seized. The spring behind it is live, so keep the slide standing on its muzzle and a hand over the cap throughout. Two millimetres is the correct punch; smaller will slip off the pin face.
deepSteps.quote: Push the safety plunger all the way down to the stop. While applying downward pressure on the safety plunger, remove the striker assembly and striker retract spring from the slide
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.2.1 Slide Disassembly, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)
deepSteps.warn: The striker assembly and its retract spring are under load. Hold the safety plunger down and control both as they come out.

deepSteps.title: Extractor pin turns 90 degrees — it does not drift straight out
deepSteps.action: Optic-ready models: take the cover or base plate off first. Hold the slide with the muzzle to the left and turn the extractor pin 90 degrees with a screwdriver into its disassembly position, so the slot in the pin lies perpendicular to the barrel.
deepSteps.prose: This is the F-Series' biggest departure from the standard PDP slide, and reaching for a punch here will simply mar the pin. The pin is keyed: until its slot is perpendicular to the barrel it is locked in the slide and no amount of drifting will move it. Turn it with a screwdriver blade that actually fills the slot, and check the orientation by eye before going further. Repeatedly pressing the extractor in helps the pin find its position if it feels stiff.
deepSteps.quote: Use a screwdriver to turn the extractor pin by 90° to the disassembly position (4.2.1 Fig. 3). The orientation of the extractor pin’s slot must be perpendicular to the barrel.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.2.1 Slide Disassembly, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)

deepSteps.title: 1 mm punch from the top, thumb on the extractor
deepSteps.action: Insert a 1 mm drift punch from the top into the small hole at the top of the slide, turn the slide upside down and hold the extractor in place with your thumb, then carefully drift the 1 mm punch in to force the extractor pin outwards.
deepSteps.prose: One millimetre is a fragile punch and the hole is a close fit, so keep it square to the slide and drive it gently — a bent punch left in that hole is a much worse problem than a dirty extractor. Your thumb on the extractor is doing real work here: the extractor is under a torsion spring and will pivot out the moment the pin clears. Once the pin starts to emerge, stop punching and pull it. The torsion spring is the part that gets lost, so watch for it as the extractor's rear end pivots clear.
deepSteps.quote: Carefully drift a 1 mm punch in (4.2.1 Fig. 4) to force the extractor pin outwards.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.2.1 Slide Disassembly, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)
deepSteps.warn: The F-Series extractor carries a TORSION spring, not the standard PDP's plunger and coil. It will fly out if the extractor is released unsupported.

deepSteps.title: F-Series extractor spring DOES come out — unlike the standard PDP
deepSteps.action: Remove the extractor spring from its seat inside the extractor slot, and keep it with the torsion spring and the safety plunger.
deepSteps.prose: This is the exact opposite of the standard PDP instruction, where the extractor spring is explicitly to be left in its slot. On the F-Series the manual directs you to take it out, so cleaning the slot properly is possible here in a way it is not on the other book's guns. Do not read across between the two manuals on this point. Lay the parts out in removal order — safety plunger and its spring, extractor, torsion spring, extractor spring — because reassembly runs safety first, then extractor, then striker.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the extractor spring from its seat inside the extractor slot (4.2.1 Fig. 5, #3).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.2.1 Slide Disassembly, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)

deepSteps.title: Reassembly order inside the slide is fixed
deepSteps.action: Put the slide back together in this order: striker safety and its plunger first, then the extractor with its torsion spring, then the striker assembly. Do not try to seat the striker before the extractor is in.
deepSteps.prose: The parts interfere with one another, so an order that feels arbitrary is actually mechanical — the striker blocks the safety, and the safety must be down before the extractor will press home. Secure the safety plunger's spring in the plunger hole with a little gun lube, never grease, to stop it falling out while you work. When the safety is assembled correctly it sits slightly BELOW the feed rib next to it; if it stands proud, it has not entered the deepest part of its blind hole. Check that before anything else goes in.
deepSteps.caution: Use gun lube, not grease, to hold the safety plunger spring in place. Grease will stay there and gum the plunger.
deepSteps.quote: Reassembly starts with the striker safety and the extractor, continue with the striker assembly.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.2.2 Slide Reassembly, note, printed p.17 (PDF p.17)

deepSteps.title: Prove the striker is home before the end cap goes on
deepSteps.action: With the safety plunger at rest, try to pull the striker assembly back out of the slide. If it comes, it is not seated. Only when it will not come out do you align its guide with the striker channel and press it home with the end cap.
deepSteps.prose: This is a real test with a definite answer, and it is the only thing standing between a correctly assembled slide and one that will not fire. Align both tabs of the striker assembly, slide the retract spring onto the striker's front end, and insert with both noses facing up while holding the safety down; then release the safety plunger and pull. A striker that slides back out has caught on the safety rather than passing under it. Reinsert the end cap from the bottom of the slide until it snaps.
deepSteps.quote: The striker assembly is correctly seated if it can no longer be pulled out of the slide while the safety plunger is in its resting position.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.2.2 Slide Reassembly, printed p.18 (PDF p.18)

deepSteps.title: Magazine strip, and the +2 tab
deepSteps.action: Depress the floorplate catch through the hole in the floorplate with a 4 mm drift punch, slide the floorplate forward off the tube while keeping the catch down, remove the catch and spring through the bottom, then turn the tube upright and take the follower out.
deepSteps.prose: Keep a thumb across the floorplate as it starts to move — the catch is the only thing restraining a 15-round spring. On a +2 magazine the sequence starts differently: find the metal tab at the rear base and, with the floorplate fully seated rearward, push it toward the top of the magazine with a flat screwdriver until it protrudes from the base, then slide the floorplate as normal. Everything goes back in exactly the orientation it came out and nothing needs force. If a part will not go, it is round the wrong way.
deepSteps.quote: Turn the tube right side up and remove the follower through the bottom of the tube.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.3.1 Magazine Disassembly, printed p.18 (PDF p.18)
deepSteps.warn: The magazine spring is under pressure. Control the floorplate catch and the spring while removing the floorplate.

deepSteps.title: 10,000 rounds: springs get replaced, not just cleaned
deepSteps.action: At about 10,000 shots, replace the recoil spring assembly, the striker retract spring and the mainspring. Field strip, remove the safety plunger then the striker assembly, take the retract spring off, and change the mainspring off the striker guide.
deepSteps.prose: Walther publishes an actual service life for the F-Series springs, which most pistol manuals do not, and ignoring it shows up as inconsistent ejection and the occasional light strike long before anything breaks. To change the mainspring, stand the striker tip on a wooden or plastic base, keep the rear end of the mainspring compressed, grasp the striker guide by its protruding projection and pivot that projection up until the guide can be removed. The striker guide itself is reusable — its rear end has indentations on the outer edge and the muzzle end is flat, so it can only go back one way. Press it on without canting until it engages.
deepSteps.quote: After 10,000 shots, it is recommended to replace the recoil spring assembly, the retract spring and mainspring.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.7 Preventive Maintenance, printed p.21 (PDF p.21)

deepSteps.title: Striker channel dry, one drop everywhere else
deepSteps.action: Clean and dry the striker channel and put no gun lubricant into it. In the slide, one drop on surface (E) and one on the safety plunger (F); on the frame, one drop on each slide guide and one on the trigger bar.
deepSteps.prose: The F-Series lubrication diagram differs from the standard PDP's — the standard book names the safety plunger and the disconnector cut, this one names surface (E) and the safety plunger (F) — so do not lubricate an F-Series from the other manual's picture. Oil in the striker channel collects unburned powder and carbon and slows the striker until primers get dented rather than struck, which reads as an ammunition fault. Wipe the barrel's external surfaces and the ramp where the locking block cams the barrel with a light film. Magazines take a film on their external metal surfaces only.
deepSteps.caution: Do not put any gun lubricant into the striker channel. Over-lubricating anywhere attracts dirt, unburned powder and carbon residue.
deepSteps.quote: Slide: Put only one drop of lubricant on surface (E) and the safety plunger (F).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — Rev.b — 4.5 Lubrication, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Brush from the CHAMBER end until the bristles fully exit at the muzzle, then pull back until they fully exit the chamber end — no reversing inside the bore
Powder-removing solvent and a brass bristle bore brush to lift lead and firing residue out of the 89 mm or 102 mm polygonal barrel
Wipe clean with patches or a swab, then a light film of gun lubricant on the barrel's external surfaces and on the ramp where the locking block cams it
Threaded-barrel guns: clean and re-check the ½"-28 UNEF thread and refit the thread protector before storage

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BREECH FACE & EXTRACTOR
tasks: Small brush in solvent around the breech face, the chamber end of the barrel, the extractor and the adjacent areas exposed to powder or primer residue
One drop of lubricant on slide surface (E) and one on the safety plunger (F) — the F-Series diagram, not the standard PDP's
Striker channel DRY: no lubricant at any point
Optic-ready models: refit the cover or base plate before the slide is cycled

cleaning.name: FRAME, BACKSTRAP & RAILS
tasks: Light brushing with solvent to lift residue off the glass-fibre reinforced polymer frame
One drop of lubricant on each slide guide and one on the trigger bar
Light film of high quality gun lubricant on all external metal surfaces, then wipe clean
The F-Series backstraps come in Small and Medium; check the fitted one is seated and its pin is home after cleaning
Cold climate: use a lubricant that will not congeal at low temperature

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Light film of gun lubricant on external metal surfaces only
Wipe the tube interior dry; oil inside collects grit and drags the follower
Inspect the feed lips and follower while the magazine is apart, and never use excessive force reassembling it
+2 magazines: hold the tab flush with the body while sliding the floorplate fully rearward, then push the tab into its correct seating

cleaning.name: SOLVENT LIMITS & SERVICE LIFE
tasks: No ammonia-based or strong alkaline solvents on any Walther firearm
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning; 50 °C (122 °F) is the ultrasonic ceiling
Log the round count — recoil spring assembly, retract spring and mainspring are replacement items at about 10,000 shots
Check the pistol for signs of wear every time it is cleaned; if wear is noted, stop using it and have it checked

reassembly: Slide upside down, barrel in with the locking lugs oriented as the manual's figure shows.

3.5" models: LARGER end of the recoil spring assembly into the spring mounting at the front of the slide. 4" models: SMALLER end of the recoil rod into that mounting. Read the barrel length off the gun, do not guess.
Insert the rear end of the spring assembly into the lower barrel recess while compressing the spring. Flex in the assembly is normal.
Push the slide onto the frame from the front until the take-down catch engages, checking the slide has also picked up the REAR slide guides, then release it fully forward into the locked position.

If the slide was opened: striker safety and plunger first, then extractor with its torsion spring and the extractor spring, then the striker assembly — and prove the striker will not pull back out before the end cap goes on.
Turn the extractor pin back with a screwdriver until its slot lies slightly toward the muzzle; pressing the extractor in repeatedly helps it orientate.
Magazine back together in original orientation, floorplate on until the catch snaps audibly.
Dry-patch the bore before the pistol is loaded.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber confirmed empty: rack the slide and let it run — it must return fully into battery unaided, with no grit or hesitation on the rails (a wrongly oriented recoil spring assembly shows up exactly here). Lock it open on the slide stop and drop it with the thumb. Insert the empty magazine and pull down on the floorplate; it should not move. With the striker cocked the take-down catch must refuse to depress; after a trigger press it should come down freely. If the slide was opened, confirm the striker assembly cannot be pulled out with the safety plunger at rest, that the safety sits slightly below the feed rib beside it, and that the extractor springs back flush when pressed. Optic-ready guns: cover or base plate fitted and tight before the pistol is fired.
